elements.text: A C++ port of Ascend/verl TransferQueue: the KV store every BluTrain RL actor writes tensors into and reads them back from

Tensors live only here, in memory. No byte cap in production, no replication: a dead shard loses its rows.

PUT_DATA · GET_DATA
(direct, never via the controller)
All links: ZMQ DEALER (client) → ROUTER (server) over tcp, ephemeral ports, custom little-endian binary messages.

1 · KV_RETRIEVE(create) → controller
keys → global ids; unknown keys get fresh ids (capacity is checked here); reply carries each id's shard and the shard registry

2 · PUT_DATA → shard(s)
new keys go to registered[hash(uid prefix) % n], so a prompt and its trajectories share a shard; rows merge per field

3 · KV_UPDATE → controller
mark the fields produced, record the shard, merge tags. Data lands before metadata: no reader sees a field before it is stored.

Two API layers — RL uses only the first

KV layer (verl v1)  —  used by RL
kv_put · kv_batch_put · kv_batch_get · kv_list · kv_clear · save_checkpoint · load_checkpoint. Rows are addressed by string keys; status lives in tags that RL interprets.

Streaming layer (original TQ)  —  compiled and tested, never called by RL
NOTIFY_DATA_UPDATE · GET_META with per-task consumption · FifoSampler / GRPOGroupNSampler · ADVANCE_VERSION · FIND_STRANDED_GROUPS.  →  page 8

Toolchain
g++ -std=c++2a -O2 -g. No msgpack or protobuf: the wire format is hand-written. Depends on libzmq + cppzmq and BluTrain's Tensor-Implementations (OwnTensor::Tensor, save/load_tensor, ThreadPool) — which pulls in the CUDA link line.

Capacity check before start
total_storage_size ≥ ceil((num_warmup_batches + 1) · train_batch_size) · (1 + rollout.n), or ≤ 0 for unlimited.  [1.5B: 20000 ≥ 2 · 32 · 9 = 576]

History
tools/ray_launcher.py used to start the colocated binary from a Python Ray actor; commit f52f57b (10-19) replaced it with the C++ RAY_REMOTE actors above.
Partitions, keys and global ids; what the controller knows about each row; how tensors and strings are serialized

shard index
where the tensors live
-1 = no data yet

Ids are global across partitions — there is one allocator. A partition is created lazily (KV_RETRIEVE with create, KV_UPDATE, …) and pre-allocates 1 id (kPreAllocSampleNum) that is never bound to a key. The uid prefix before the first '_' is what routes a key to a shard, so RL uids contain '-' but never '_'.
DataPartitionStatus — the controller's view of one partition
which ids have each field — per-field production
shard holding the row (-1 if absent)
one merged tag map per key
Per-field production, e.g. after rollout + trainer

scan_data_status(fields, task) returns ids produced for ALL requested fields and not yet consumed by that task. Asking for {rm_scores, old_log_probs} → ids 1, 2. A field never produced anywhere in the partition → empty. (The KV path doesn't use this — RL reads tags instead.)
Tags — small metadata merged per key
serialize_batch — the bytes of a PUT_DATA payload

The buffer is pre-sized exactly (serialized_batch_size) — VectorWriteBuf throws if the estimate is wrong. Host-endian raw writes. load_tensor copies every tensor on read. "TNS0" encodes an invalid tensor.
Strings ride as "bytes tensors": 1-D UInt8, marker 0xB7 first

bytes_tensor("72") = UInt8[3]. The marker is the only check (tensor_bytes throws without it). RL sends prompt_text, ground_truth, data_source and extra_fields (JSON) this way; only the field name says it's text.
FieldDtype (u8, 18 values): Int8…Int64, UInt8…UInt64, Bfloat16, Float16, Float32, Float64, Bool, Complex32/64/128, Float4_e2m1(_2x)
One Message type, a hand-rolled binary codec, and a ZMQ ROUTER reactor feeding four worker threads

header
Message with an empty payload slot

DEALER clients send 2 frames (header with SNDMORE, then payload); the ROUTER sees 3. Anything that isn't exactly 3 frames is dropped silently — the client just times out. Payloads ≥ 4096 bytes go out zero-copy (zmq_msg_init_data with a free callback).
Message header — fields in encode order (explicit little-endian; strings = u32 length + bytes)
blue = used by the KV path · grey = streaming / bookkeeping. request_id = 8 random hex chars; every RPC is one Message in, one Message out.

ThreadPool
kWorkerThreads = 4
deserialize → handle_request
→ time into stats[type]

Only the reactor touches the ROUTER socket; up to 4 handlers run at once per server. A handler exception becomes REQUEST_ERROR{success=false, error_message} — and isn't counted in stats. The controller's handlers then serialize on Controller::mutex_, so 4 threads mostly buy overlap with shard RPCs inside KV_CLEAR and checkpoints.

Client side — TransferQueueRpcClient(id, address, timeout 5000 ms)
Its own zmq context + DEALER (rcvtimeo, linger 0). One outstanding request, no request_id matching, no retries. On timeout it rebuilds the socket so a late reply can't answer the next call, then throws. KVClient raises the timeout to 60 s.

Each request type has a matching _RESPONSE (HANDSHAKE → HANDSHAKE_ACK; NOTIFY_DATA_UPDATE → _ACK / _ERROR), plus REQUEST_ERROR. Unhandled types get REQUEST_ERROR "… has no handler for request_type X". Clients turn success=false into runtime_error("…server reported failure: …").
The KV operations RL calls, step by step — KVClient::kv_batch_put, kv_batch_get and kv_list
kv_batch_put("train", ["u1_0_0", "u1_1_0"], rows {X, Y}, tags {status: success})  — a worked example
Fresh store, shards {0, 1}. Everything below happens under KVClient::mutex_: one request in flight per client.
takes CheckpointGate shared; capacity check: live keys + new > max → "TransferQueue full …"
partition created → pre-allocates id 0; the two keys get ids 1 and 2
both keys share prefix "u1" → one shard, one RPC; rows merge per field
try_put_data: never blocks (no byte cap in production)
production_by_field_[X], [Y] += {1,2}; shard, version 0, produced_at; merge tags
only now can a reader see X and Y for these keys

Later, the trainer writes advantages for u1_0_0
KV_RETRIEVE finds id 1 with shard s → PUT_DATA with only {advantages} to shard s (merged into the existing row) → KV_UPDATE with fields [advantages]. Keys keep their shard for life.

Tags-only put (rows empty) — status flips like {status: running}
KV_RETRIEVE(create) → KV_UPDATE with tags and no fields. No shard is contacted, so it works even with zero shards. RL's async_kv_put is std::async around this: it frees the caller but adds no throughput.
Routing: which shard gets a new key?

A prompt row and all its trajectories land together. std::hash is unseeded — stable within one build only — which is fine because the choice is stored at the controller once made. If the shard count changes, only new keys route differently. (Example assignment illustrative.)

kv_batch_get(partition, keys, select_fields)
1. KV_RETRIEVE(create=0) — not gated, not counted against capacity
2. one GET_DATA per shard with the deduplicated ids and select_fields (empty = all fields)
Unknown keys are left out; a known key with no shard yet comes back as an empty Record. Nothing is marked consumed.

kv_list(partition, filter?)
One KV_LIST returns every key + its tags (no tensors, hash-map order). The filter runs client-side in rl::TQClient, so each ReplayBufferAsync poll costs O(keys in the partition). RL tells prompt rows from trajectories by the tag is_prompt == true.

Not transactional: a put is 3 separate RPCs. A failure in between leaves keys created with no data (still counted toward capacity) or rows on a shard that the controller never marked. And because a status tag and the trajectory rows are written by different calls, a reader can see "finished" before the rows are visible — RL's replay buffer treats such groups as "unsettled".
Where SampleIds come from, when they are reused, and the race that the release_cleared fix closed
PartitionIndexManager — one allocator for all partitions

allocate_indexes("train", 4)
  → 4, 7, 2  (free list first, FIFO)
  → 9        (then mint next_index_++ → 10)

release_indexes(p, ids)   // throws if any id isn't owned,
                          // checked before any change
release_partition(p)      // frees all of p's ids
adopt_indexes(…)          // checkpoint restore
Ids never shrink and there is no compaction — the u64 space doesn't run out, which is why leaking ids after a failed clear is an acceptable trade.

max_kv_samples_ = total_storage_size [20000]; 0 = unlimited.
Checked only in KV_RETRIEVE(create=1): if live keys + new keys > max it throws
"TransferQueue full: N samples held, M new key(s) would exceed total_storage_size=X -- clear consumed groups first".
No blocking, no eviction; updating existing keys still works. Live keys = Σ key_count over partitions (pre-allocated ids don't count).
live keys held   →   a put that crosses the line fails at step 1; kv_clear makes room
CLEAR_DATA(partition, ids)  — new client, 5 s timeout
grouped by shard; whole rows dropped

Controller::kv_clear
under the mutex: unbind keys, erase production / shard / tags. Ids NOT freed yet.

release_cleared(partition, ids)
only if every shard succeeded → the ids go back on the free list. Otherwise they stay out of circulation for good (a deliberate leak).
The race it fixed  (commit bc15fd9, "Bug 2" in GRPO_1P5B_REPORT.md)
CLEAR_DATA id 17 lands — wipes the new row
After: release only once the shard row is gone
the next put may now reuse 17 safely
Symptom: "finished groups are missing DAPO metric 'reward'" — or, because shard puts merge, a row holding a mix of two trajectories.
Still unfixed: CLEAR_PARTITION calls release_partition (Controller.cpp:250) BEFORE clear_on_shards — the same reuse race. RL doesn't use it during training.
StorageServer + SimpleStorageManager: in-memory rows, merged field by field

One mutex + a condition variable per shard. Data is in memory only (plus checkpoint files). A Record is an unordered_map<string, OwnTensor::Tensor>. There's no device handling: save_tensor copies GPU tensors to CPU.
try_put_data: merge each listed field into the row; never blocks. No schema check.
the requested fields (empty = whole row); missing ids skipped
erase whole rows, drop empty partitions, notify_all
Merge per field, and net-byte accounting

net new bytes = Σ over (id, field)  max(0, new.nbytes − existing.nbytes)
              = max(0, 3 − 2) + max(0, 2 − 0) = 3 KB      // not 5 KB

if capacity_bytes > 0:
    net > capacity            → invalid_argument ("can never fit, even empty")
    current + net > capacity  → try_put_data returns false → "storage full …"
else:                           // capacity_bytes = 0 — what RL and the binary use
    always fits

The net-bytes rule came from commit 72bc934 ("fixed_storage"); before it, overwriting a field counted its full size again. Servers always call the non-blocking try_put_data, so a full shard can't park one of its 4 worker threads (regression-tested).

No byte cap in production: SimpleStorageManager() defaults to capacity_bytes = 0 in both TQStorageActor and storage_server_main. The only limit is the controller's key count, so a shard can grow until the process runs out of memory.
save_checkpoint / load_checkpoint: one controller file, one file per shard, and an all-or-nothing load

shared
KV_UPDATE · KV_CLEAR · CLEAR_PARTITION
NOTIFY_DATA_UPDATE · KV_RETRIEVE(create=1)

not gated
KV_RETRIEVE(create=0) · KV_LIST · GET_META
shard PUT_DATA / GET_DATA

Writer-preferring: once a save is waiting, new shared holders queue behind it. Shard PUT_DATA isn't gated, so a row written mid-save can appear in a shard file without metadata — checkpoint_inspect calls these "harmless orphan rows".

SAVE_CHECKPOINT → each shard
shard-<i>.tqsh (30 min timeout)

Client side: KVClient builds a temporary RpcClient with a 1 h timeout (kCheckpointTimeoutMs). Not saved: consumption state, group ids, produced_at (reset at load), declared schema, streaming-layer samples.
parse into staged_, live rows untouched
if any shard fails: ABORT_LOAD_CHECKPOINT to the staged ones, throw "… nothing loaded"
1. parse_kv_checkpoint — magic, format, every shard listed. 2. deployed shard set must EQUAL the saved one, else "nothing loaded". Controller state untouched so far.

3. apply_kv_checkpoint — drop all partitions, set the version, adopt_indexes for every restored id BEFORE re-creating partitions (so the new pre-allocated id can't collide), rebind keys, re-mark production, merge tags.
Known gap (ponytail comment): a shard that dies between stage and commit stays stale while the others commit. Headers are host-endian.

controller.tqck   (format 2)
"TQCK" | u32 format | i64 current_version
       | u32 n_shards | i32 shard_idx[n]  (sorted)
       | u32 n_records
       | repeat: u64 len + Message(KV_UPDATE, sender "checkpoint")
// one record per (partition, produced-field set):
// keys, sample_ids, fields, tags, shard indices, versions

shard-<i>.tqsh   (format 1)
"TQSH" | u32 format | u32 n_partitions
       | repeat: u32 id_len, id, u64 len,
                 serialize_batch(rows of that partition)
// serialized under the lock, written outside it,
// .tmp then rename

checkpoint_inspect <dir>  — read-only dump + consistency check
The original TransferQueue model — consumption-tracked GET_META and samplers. Still compiled and tested; RL never calls it.

select_and_consume(partition, fields, task, sampler, batch_size):   // under the controller mutex
    ready  = scan_data_status(fields, task)    // produced for all fields, not consumed by task
    groups = group_id of each ready id
    chosen = sampler.sample(ready, groups, batch_size)
    mark_consumed(task, chosen)                // per task_name; RESET_CONSUMPTION clears

Controller GET_META returns metadata only (ids, their shards, the shard registry, versions) — data comes from GET_DATA. The legacy colocated TransferQueueServer returns data inline instead, and has no KV ops. Quirk: TransferQueueRpcClient::get() against a ControllerServer throws "truncated" on the empty payload.

Sorts ids, buckets them by non-empty group_id (lexicographic group order), takes the first n of each complete group. Needs batch_size / n = 2 complete groups here — if it can't find them all it returns nothing (all-or-nothing). Throws if n = 0 or batch_size % n ≠ 0.

FifoSampler — the one always installed on ControllerServer
Takes the first min(batch_size, n) ids in the order given. That order is unordered_set iteration order, so it is not FIFO in insertion order.

find_stranded(max_age_ms) — GRPOGroupNSampler only
Groups with an empty id or fewer than n members whose oldest produced_at is at least max_age_ms old → StrandedGroup{group_id, ids, oldest_age_ms}. FifoSampler returns none.

Versions
current_version_ starts at 0 and only ADVANCE_VERSION bumps it; every production update is stamped with it. RL never advances it, so all RL samples are version 0 — staleness lives in RL's global_steps tags instead.

Why RL doesn't use this layer: verl v1 moved to the KV API, and BluTrain's ReplayBufferAsync re-implements verl's staleness/DAPO eviction and oldest-first sampling on top of kv_list. The Makefile notes that the RankAwareSampler was removed ("Phase 4") in favour of write-time routing by GroupRouter.
Observability, what the 16 test suites cover, measured numbers, and the known gaps

MetricsHttpServer
Raw POSIX socket, HTTP/1.0, one connection at a time, polls every 200 ms. Answers any path with text/plain; version=0.0.4 (500 on a render error). Each scrape synchronously sends GET_STATS to every shard with a 2 s timeout. Enabled by transfer_queue.metrics.enabled [true].
Logging: none. The library never writes to stderr; binaries print only their address. Errors are exceptions on the client or REQUEST_ERROR / success=false on the wire.

(150 ms poll interval)

• 1–64 MB single-key writes: 322–542 MB/s, none rejected (no byte cap)
• cap 5, 16 concurrent clients: exactly 5 succeed, 27 rejected
• 200 rows settled in 0.051 s (~3925 rows/s): 16 replicas, 16 workers, 4 shards

Partition clear race
CLEAR_PARTITION frees ids before clearing shards (unfixed; unused in training).

No byte cap
Shards are unbounded in production; only the key count is limited.

Not transactional
A put is 3 RPCs; failures leave orphan keys or rows. No retries anywhere.

Single copy, in memory
No replication or restart, though the requirements doc asks for both.

One request per client
KVClient serializes everything on one mutex; a fresh ZMQ context per RpcClient.

Controller ceiling
4 workers + one global mutex, blocking shard RPCs in clears — unmeasured at scale.

kv_list is O(keys)
Every replay-buffer poll fetches the whole partition and filters client-side.

Stale shard cache
KVClient keeps a shard's old address if it re-registers elsewhere.

Docs vs code: TQ/README.md is empty; docs cited in comments are missing; RL/STATUS.md notes the `vv` branch pins the submodule at f52f57b — before the checkpoint (d4a3b85), net-bytes (72bc934) and release_cleared (bc15fd9) fixes.
